reviews.comment: Tries but not the best at teaching, when I took it the reviews said only take if you already know calc, I agree it is way easier if you're already introduced to topics beforehand, you will study a lot yourself to get A's but most people don't fully pay attention and end up doing that anyway.

Once one understands that Calculus in College is somewhat different from what one was used from high school, one can get used to the 
new pace. He understands that and helps you to make that jump. Was always available outside class.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Schlumprecht is a nice professor and overall a nice guy, however his course was confusing. He was constantly backtracking due to an error made in his lectures, and he'd often wouldn't explain what he was doing. He erases work before you have the opportunity to write things down, and it's difficult to ask questions.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He's very nice, but he lowk sucks at teaching. Didn't answer questions well at all. He has bad handwriting, an accent that you have to get used to, and he makes lots of mistakes. Quizzes very fairly easy but he graded hard on tests. This class is not at all similar to AP Calc AB or BC so be ready for that.
RMP won't let me say what I really want to say. I wouldn't take this class again, this class makes my high school math teacher seem like genius.

While you can tell that Schlumprecht cares, he is not very good at teaching. He rambles, makes countless mistakes, doesn't answer questions well, and is a bit all over the place. I think if you've taken calc before, you will be fine. The class itself wasn't difficult, but if this is your first time taking calc, it seemed to be a struggle.

Dr. Schlumrpecht is a very kind person, but he is not good at explaining introductory calc. If you've never learned calculus before, try to find another prof. If you're unable to, please find other resources to help teach you because his lectures + notes will not be sufficient. Quiz questions are taken directly from practice problems in the notes.
A lot of Theorems and Definitions, you need to learn, but he is very accessible.

Professor Schlumprecht is very knowledgeable and kind. However, I would only take this course if you already have experience in calculus. Lectures are fast paced, his handwriting isn't the greatest, and he has an accent that can take some time to get used to. I failed the first exam badly, but with lots of effort, I finished with an A in the class.

I almost Q dropped after the first exam, it was very difficult  at the beginning. But Professor Schlumprecht, was  very  accessible 
during office hours, and after some time I started to understand and enjoy his class.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The lectures are pretty much useless. Bad handwriting and a slight accent can make things difficult to understand. Often made mistakes in class and was only pointed out if a student caught it. The majority of my learning came from the MLC help sessions. Go to the help sessions if you're struggling!!! Would recommend taking a different professor.

His lectures are decent, a little fast but you'll get used to the pace. Quizzes and practice problems are extremely easy, which ends up being a problem. The tests are super hard, and the lack of practice exams nor relevant practice problems make them near impossible to study for. Schlumprecht is helpful, but you need to be really good at Calc.

Dr. Thomas is a very wonderful and caring guy. However that doesn't make him the best teacher. I had to drop his class he has a quiz every friday about the previous weeks material so you are juggling 2 weeks of material at the same time. No homework but that doesn't make it good cause you don't know what to do. Take only if you a Calculus God.
Schlumprecht explains concepts well and the class is well thought too. Exams are very similar to practice tests with most questions pulled from the practice exam
If you get past his accent, he's a great teacher and the class itself is fairly easy. Tests are very similar to practice exams and he explains concepts fairly well

His online textbook is actually very helpful and provides a lot of examples and practice problems. His lectures were a little hard to follow along with, but with the help of the textbook the content wasn't too bad. His old exams are online and are super helpful for studying for exams. Had to put in the work, but ended up getting an A.

I had As in calculus AB&BC but since im applied math, I had to take this class. I barely got out with a B. do not take him if you don't have to. his exams are nothing like the practice ones. he picks on students and would often call this one guy in our class "slow". I do not recommend him if you're trying to have a smooth first semester.

Take him if you took calculus in HS and have a good understand of the content overall
DO NOT risk taking him if you want to go med school (take the other math course) or you aren't physics or stats majors. Lots of HW on webassign. He's very nice :) and gives generous curves :D (The final was lowkey very difficult but we don't talk about that)

I honestly hate to give such a low rating because Dr. Schlumprecht is a very passionate helpful person, but sadly he just does not know how to teach very well. I had to rely on sources outside of class to even strugle through this class. Unless you have a strong understanding of calculus then you should not take this class.

Schlumprecht knows his stuff regarding calculus. However, most of the class (including myself) did not take high school calculus and his lectures were very confusing for us. He does not go over any steps involving problems and instead assumes you know how to do them in your head. I do not recommend if you have never taken a Calculus class before!

He moves fast through lectures, making quite a few mistakes that are noticed either by him or by students. A lot of my studying was done through outside sources, notes from hs calc, mainly YouTube vids. Exams are very short, but he does give partial credit and theres a lot of hw to balance your grade. He's very smart, just not the best teacher.

One of the funniest and most knowledgeable profs I've ever had. Super smart, but teaches super fast with a somewhat noticeable accent and if you aren't able to keep up it's easy to get lost. His class was really difficult and almost didn't cinch the A, but in the end he made the final super super easy though. Was always available for office hours.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you you are a Bioscience major, who wants to get an  easy A, which you need to go to med school, and this is your last Math class I recommend: Don't take him, take Math 147. This is a class for Math, Physics and Stat majors. You should have had high school Calculus, but this class far beyond
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Schlumprecht had a tough class, he kinda just sped ran his lectures as fast as he could.  With the practice problems on his lecture he wasn't really clearly on how to solve them, he just solved it his way, and sometimes he was wrong himself. I really wouldn't recommend him, but if you have to then go ahead.
gave points after semester but class and test were very difficult

The beginning of the semester was rough trying to get used to his teaching style. He moves very fast and even though I've taken Calc 1 before, it was challenging. However, his quizzes were very easy as they were exactly from the lecture. He truly does care about his students and will help if you need it. The final was exactly like the practice.

This professor gives great lectures, although he does make mistakes from time to time, which can confuse you when you are doing homework or taking a test or quiz. Also, the answer keys to the homeworks sometimes have mistakes which can also be confusing, especially when a different answer was given by the professor, the key, and the TA.

f this is your first time learning the material, I wouldn't recommend. Schlumprecht was nice and cared about his students, but he was kind of all over the place during his lectures. They were hard to follow along. Also, he frequently made mistakes grading exams and in his lecture notes. Quiz every Friday and three exams plus a mandatory final.
reviews.ratingTags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class was certainly a rollercoaster for me as I assumed I can wing it after taking AP Calc in HS- but I was wrong. AP Calc will help with this class, but this is college-level calc for math majors. Dr. Schlumprecht was very patient and kind during office hours. Maybe there's a slight language barrier with explanations but mans trying his best.
Great prof, changed my major to math because of him.

Dr. Schlumprecht wants you to understand the concepts of Mathematics, and he cares about  teaching them to 
you. But I guess, reading some of the previous comments,  he was unsuccessful. It seems that some of my class mates think that what they were taught in high school, is enough. And having been successful there entitles them to an A in college.

It was not an easy class, but Dr. Schlumprecht did a good job to make it accessible. He cared for his students,  was willing to explain the same problem many times until every body understood it. A comment to some of the previous comments: they sound bitter, written by people who thought they knew it all, because they had Calc  in high school

He's a really nice professor and really does want you to understand the stuff, but he's difficult to follow and overcomplicates everything. I took calculus in high school and finished with an A in the class and a 3 on the AP exam, but the way he teaches things makes it very difficult and for no reason! Needless to say, I wouldn't recommend him.

I have taken calculus already and this class was mad hard. This guy does not know how to teach properly and is in his own world. He is talking to himself and no one understands what he is saying. You should look at the students faces when he is uttering nonsense. Hilarious! Someone who has gotten a 5 on the calc ap exam should not be struggling.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The previous comments are unfair, probably most of them are  students who should have taken precalc first, or easier classes like 151 or 141, and not calculus for math majors. Dr. Schlumprecht was a good prof. Maybe a bit on the theoretical side, but he was very accessible for any questions, and put a lot of effort in explaining us the theory.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Not funny at all. His logic makes no sense. If your degree requirement says to take Math 171, you can take Math 151 as a substitute. Advisors won't tell you this because then their 171 classes won't fill up. Take your ap credit for this class, advisors will recommend not to so you can get "a solid foundation in calculus". They just want your money!

His class is all theoretical based. We only do 2 example problems every class because he spends all of his time proving all the theorems in calculus. We don't even need to know how to prove the theorems, but he waste all of class time trying to prove them. Answers keys are wrong half the time and he solves some of the questions wrong on the board

I already did calc 1 in high school, but this guy somehow made it so hard and complicated that even I didn't understand. You have to memorize theorems word for word and there is no partial credit at all in his class. Weekly quizzes on Fridays. He gives a review for the exam that is nothing like the exam. AVOID this guy at all cost.

I feel bad because he really is a nice and sweet guy. As others said, he just can't convey his thoughts well. He reads off his notes without explaining in detail. Most of us have a poor foundation in pre-calculus, which he needs to be aware of. You're only graded by weekly quizzes and the 4 exams. TAKE 151 OR 142 IF YOU CAN!!!

Hes a great guy. He just cant articulate his thoughts very well. This class is much harder than other cal classes because of how theory heavy it is. He mainly just reads off of his notes and explanations are not clear. He seems to care though and if you go to his office hours he tries to help. He is just unable to explain topics well.

Seem like a nice guy although my friends have had mixed experience as well as the 2 diff sections so its hard to give a fair review. Lectures are basically the notes, hes got one of the worst handwritings tho. Very clear about stuff. Final was optional since he prob figured nobody wants to learn cal and write proofs... But yea, decent is prob fair

Really nice professor, wants us to understand, but lectures can be quite a bore just due to content. If in MATH409, memorize all definitions, theorems, AND proofs. Like, make notecards and fill in the blanks for yourself to memorize. One wrong symbol, and the whole thing could be wrong. Straightforward class, just lots of content.

This class was fairly straight forward and test heavy. The homework was the best way to learn the material as the lectures could be confusing at times between technical difficulties and a slight (but understandable) accent. I mainly taught myself the information which was fine considering I took calculus in high school.

He isn't the best professor when initially teaching a topic because he's very smart but he can't convey his thoughts very easily. But if you ask him to slow down he is more than willing to answer any questions you have and doesn't move on until you get it. Exams are easy to prepare for with past exams, so getting an A is very feasible.

He can be hard to understand at times because of his accent. He moves pretty fast. He posts his lecture notes online so if you miss you can catch up, but you get a lot more by going to class than reading the notes. Attendance is not mandatory though. Weekly quizzes, two tests and a final, hw not graded. Recitation helps more than the actual class.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I liked the class. At the beginning I was overwhelmed by the amount of definitions and theorems he made us learn, and he asked them in weekly quizzes and on tests. But after a while it started to make sense. In class he moves at a fast pace, to cover all the material. But when you visit him in his office he will take all the time you need.

Moves at quick pace and doesn't stop to review often. While textbook isn't required, the optional homework is there which if you ignore, you won't pass. He's nice and knows what he's talking about but isn't great at explaining to where we understand the material. Frustratingly definition and theorem heavy. Google and YouTube will be your friends
Great prof, explains well, but a bit on the theoretical side
reviews.ratingTags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Schlumprect is an awesome guy. He tells funny stories during class, and is clearly very invested in the students learning. The tests are hard, but if you go to class and pay attention and study you should be fine.

I love this prof! I took him for MATH 171/172. He's a really nice guy and will try his best to help you out. His class is a lot of work though. If you are willing to put in the work, getting an A or B should be easy. He can be a bit confusing at times, so just let him know and he will try his best to explain better. His notes are also posted online

3 tests, including final, each worth 25% of grade. Quizzes every week but they are questions pulled directly from the homework, not collected only for practice. Schlump is not really that good but he could be worse and he was the only MATH 171 prof available this semester. Tests are hard, study more than just the study guide. He is a nice person.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: You get out of this class what you put in. Homework is optional, but you have to do it in order to perform well on the quizzes and tests. There is a quiz every Friday, but otherwise attendance isn't mandatory. He's not the best at explaining, but YouTube is very helpful! He's fun in class, and I would recommend him. Put in lots of hard work though!

I had taken calculus before I got to college, so that knowledge definitely helped me get an A. To be honest, I did not think he was that great at explaining confusing topics; however, he is extremely nice. I enjoyed being in his class for the semester. You will have to work hard for a good grade, but it is doable.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough Grader--Tests? Not many--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Great Class, but only if you like a bit of Theory and proofs

I am not sure which class the previous commentator attended, certainly not Dr. Schlumprecht's class. His notes are great, judge for yourself : shorter and easier to read than the book. Maybe a bit theoretical, with proofs. All supposedly undoable problems were done in class and solutions to them are given. Great class!

I would NOT recommend this prof if math is not your strong suit. His accent is very heavy, notes are messy/confusing, and unneccesary homework e v e r y week. There are about 30 problems from the notes plus 30 problems and a quiz every week. 7/8 of the problems you do are impossible and irrelevant for the tests/quiz.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He is a wonderful guy, but be prepared to work in any of his classes. He's willing to work with you if you go to office hours, and expects you to be active in his class. Homework is very hard and counts for most of his class. Tests are pretty fair. Curves alot at the end.
Great prof. Has good presence, likes his job, and is really good at it. Kind of funny sometimes, too. Just don't expect it to be easy.
Great teacher, tries to make you understand the concept (and sometimes he even succeeds). If you get lost don't wait until it is tho late, and visit his office.
The class is extremely challenging. The professor is a genius and doesnt always realize his students arent as smart as him. Tests are difficult but do-able.

Great teacher. Study the reviews he gives and you'll do great. Final was exactly like past common exams he gives you to review. Usually 10pt curves. Gives quizzes every Friday over homework from the week before. I would definitely take his class again. He makes everything very clear and is always willing to review in class. Go to office hours, too!

Honestly, if you live and breathe Calculus, you will do great. He is pretty confusing only because he'll write down the wrong thing on the board and confuse himself. Also, he may mistype questions or answers on the test  - though he will give extra bonus points for finding it. Knows his stuff super well though and is beyond intelligent. Good luck!
Concerned that student understand, funny, entertaining
Very concerned whether students understand, very approachable, funny, makes classes interesting, even if it is Calculus
Very friendly, always helpful,   concerned if students understood. Sometimes a bit too much on the theoretical side, but what else can you expect from a Math prof….
Very friendly, encourages to ask questions ("you can ask whatever you want, you paid  for it"). Good preparation sheets for exams, but asks you to state definitions and theorems on tests.

One of the best professors i had at Texas A&M. Very entertaining class. Picked on me lot often. We had back and forth humorous interaction. If you want an 'A' start on the review as soon as possible.He has two test, one final and 10 quiz. Test are out of 110. so you only need a 80% to get an A.
I really love his teaching style. He is really likes teaching and funny. If you want to receive an A just visit him in his office hours.

Overall a great professor! His class is a little difficult, but I did very well with studying. He is very humorous, so I am always entertained. He has an awesome German accent, but he is definitely not difficult to understand at all. I wish I could take him again.

Overall great professor.  Sometimes difficult to follow as he goes through proofs, but always willing to take questions.  Office hours visits are helpful, A+ was helpful, when it comes to tests study exclusively the material on his prep sheets. I scored a low C on my first test and still able to rebound and score an A in the class. Very fair prof.
Demanding but helpfull

Attendance not mandatory,  but he gives pop quizzes almost weekly, asking material covered the last hour. But quizzes are  very highly  curved. Does every thing to make you learn the material beyond simply knowing how to do the problems. Overall very good class.
Instead of teaching you how to do the problems, he wants you to memorize the theory. For each test we needed to learn a page or two of definitions and theorems.
great class!
Does not know how to communicate with students on their level. Does not understand why students don't get what is going on.
He even makes Calculus entertaining
Great Guy
